answer.rationale: Constraints eliminate most directions before evidence even matters: rollback_release is ruled out by compliance (memory_b1 is therefore moot, however clean that precedent was); regional_failover (memory_b2) shifted traffic during a latency degradation but that episode was not at settlement peak with heavy writes, and cutting regions mid-peak risks exactly the thing the objective forbids — losing in-flight customer writes; enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) worked by failing fast on a *partner dependency* outage, which here would shed customer writes rather than protect them, and the current symptom is our own write-path saturation, not an upstream partner failure. That leaves relieving load on the primary or adding capacity. memory_b5 is the closest structural match to the present failure mode — read/report load contending with the primary and write latency recovering once reads were moved off — so I intend route_read_replicas. I want b5's original record because the consolidated line asserts same-day recovery causally; I need to see whether the primary was actually contended by read traffic (as here) or whether something else was concurrently changed, and whether that incident was at peak write volume. I want b3 as the runner-up because add_capacity is my fallback, and the consolidated wording says headroom was provisioned *before* the retail peak — if the source confirms it was pre-provisioned rather than added under live load, add_capacity is not actually available as a same-window intervention today and the fallback collapses. Uncertainty I am not resolving: I do not know whether report/dashboard read traffic is a material share of current primary load, and the 90-minute ramp is also consistent with a regression in the 2-hour-old release that I cannot revert — the staged-gating precedent (memory_b6) shows regressions do reach us, and if this is code-level write amplification, offloading reads only buys time and the real fix waits for the next window. Downstream value risk: moving reads to replicas puts settlement and reconciliation views behind replica lag, so a component that reads-then-writes can act on stale balances and silently corrupt money movement — worse than latency. Hence small_guarded_test: shift only clearly read-only reporting/dashboard queries, exclude anything on the settlement read-then-write path, watch replica lag and write p99 together, and keep the whole change one-command reversible rather than declaring victory from a single archived precedent.
